title: Solo dev here — I used AI to design characters for my beat 'em up game SLAMTOWN. Here's the full process behind enemy #2 (Enforcer)
author: PairOfPixelsGS
selftext:
Solo dev here - I've been designing one of the enemies of my 2.5D beat 'em up game **SLAMTOWN**. I'd like to take the opportunity to share a bit of my process for art design so it can be useful for someone, and would be very valuable to get some feedback as well. First of all, I'm a software developer for 20 years, and I'm not an artist at all, so I'm using AI, but not blindly. It's kind of my partner and helper (Ha, no solo dev then! Got me) That's what is making this project even possible. My main effort is to make it look natural and coherent throughout the entire game, and that's definitely the hardest challenge. So let's go with the process I'm following:

**#1**: Write down the character. For every character I write these sections:

**Basic Info**: role, health (From Very Low to Very High), damage, speed, equipment.

**Who they are**: very brief description of the character

**SLAMCORP Role**: all the game revolves around this big corporation SLAMCORP, who owns the streets. So every character is somehow related to the company. This is important later for the game lore

**Motivation**: nothing much to say, every character needs a motivation

**Personality**: small bullet points of how the character thinks and acts. Ambitious, Loyal, No Trash Talk, No emotion, are other examples

**Combat Behavior**: how the character behaves when it's on the scene: more defensive, more offensive, can grab player, smart (can flank players), dumb (just walk and punch), etc.

**Visual Identity**: characteristics that are exclusive to that character and differentiates him from the others. I do this as a set of elements that are part of the character. Example:

|Element|Description|
|:-|:-|
|Build|Big, trained, intimidating — former cop physique|
|Armor|SWAT-like Riot gear|
|Shield|Riot shield|
|Weapon|Baton|
|Head|Cap|

**Color direction**: the color palette of the character. Example: Dark blue, black (main colors), orange (details). I used this section to also add some visual details that would make the character feel less artificial. E.g:  Official, institutional look, worn and used, working cops, not parade units

**#2**: Send to Midjourney. I use it to generate the 2D art. Basically I start with something like: *Full-body concept art character design for "The Enforcer," a heavy tank security enemy for a wrestling beat 'em up video game...* and then I just paste all the information above in the prompt

It generates 4 examples, so I pick the best one. If I don't feel satisfied, I rerun and generate again. This is the first version:

https://preview.redd.it/mmy77djqqg6h1.png?width=896&format=png&auto=webp&s=5a511ef2613b3f616cd291c45e4bc877b5a743b4

Pretty cool, but we can clearly see the "AI signs" here: strange non-existent characters, the bag on the waist feels odd, the right boot is also not perfect. The shield and the baton are also not correct, but it's a perfect start.

**Pro tip**: to keep consistency among all the characters of the game, I use the same seed for every character, and also the Style Reference feature of Midjourney. I can elaborate better on this if you want.

**#3**: Send to Gemini: it's one of the few main AI tools to manipulate images decently. I use it to correct the imperfections on the image. Just normal prompts like:

*do these changes only:*

*- remove the shield from the image*

*- remove the yellow card on the chest that is written "ENFORCER"*

*- remove the side bag on the right side (waist)"*

I keep prompting and correcting the imperfections. This is the final result

https://preview.redd.it/624mqbyirg6h1.png?width=1024&format=png&auto=webp&s=6d8fc2dab8fba7753c39072016abc5ccc9243a2a

**Pro tip**: the more you prompt for the same image, the worse it gets in quality (at least for Gemini). If that happens, there are two ways I handle it: #1 copy the image and open a new agent. #2 use an Upscale AI Tool (I recommend Magnific, but I use Midjourney's upscale as I'm already paying for it, but I feel Magnific delivers better results).

The next step is sending this to Meshy to generate the 3D model — happy to do a follow up post on that part of the pipeline if there is interest.

Trailer drops Monday (June 15th) if you want to see these guys in action.

comments.author: 4neodesigns
comments.body: Chat get image 2 does a good job now following iterations and consistent styles. I am about to get corrections and new characters in a single chat. Can get 10 plus characters and revisions in same chat, now I do use the project so my style and references are saved in there too.

comments.author: MosesSecondofHisName
comments.body:
Nice work! The design is really cool--reminds me of old school Street Fighter characters.

I noticed the shadow on the new version lools the same as the shadow on the old version, even though the design has changed. May wanna take a look at that.

Otherwise, good stuff. I like the approach you're using too.

replies.author: PairOfPixelsGS
replies.body: Thanks for the response! And my inspiration for my first character was Ryu from SF4! You nailed it! Then I used my first hero as a style reference for the others, including this. Regarding the shadow you are totally right! That’s exactly why a manual verification is still important. Good catch.
